_README: Copy this file to add a new actuator. Delete any field you do not have a
real number for -- the tool will estimate it and flag it in the report.
Do NOT invent values just to fill the file in; an honest gap is far more
useful than a plausible-looking fabrication, because the sensitivity
analysis can only warn you about gaps it knows about.
Every field accepts either a bare number or an object with provenance:
"units":  ALWAYS state these. A unit from the wrong dimension is a hard
error; a missing one is assumed canonical SI and flagged in the
report's UNIT AUDIT. Set "strict_units": true to reject bare
numbers outright. You may also put the unit in the field name,
MINIMUM VIABLE ENTRY: mass, dims_mm, gear_ratio, one of Ke/Kt, and the
two current ratings. Everything else has a defensible default.
name: Vendor Model 123
_datasheet_README: WHICH vendor document you read these numbers out of. Vendors reissue
datasheets in place -- same title, often the same stated version -- so
without this an entry cannot be re-checked once the source has moved on.
revision  the vendor's own stamp, if any (filename date, 'Rev C', ...)
version   from the document's internal version-history page, if it has one
file      matching PDF in db/datasheets/ (gitignored; local copies only)
sha256    of that file -- the ONLY identity that cannot be faked or reused
retrieved when you downloaded it, ISO 8601
Vendor version fields are often unreliable (the four RobStride manuals all
claim v1.0 on the same date despite differing file stamps), which is why the
entry_revision is when YOU last edited this file, which is not the same as
when the datasheet was issued. Bump it whenever you change a value.
_torque_constant_pick_ONE: Ke_Vrms_per_kRPM (preferred), or Ke, or Kt_rotor, or Kt_out_per_Arms

Ke_Vrms_per_kRPM.note: line-to-line RMS volts per 1000 ROTOR rpm

Kt_out_per_Arms.note: if the datasheet quotes Kt after the gearbox

R_phase.note: LINE-TO-NEUTRAL at 25 degC. A line-to-line datasheet value is 2x this. THE single highest-value measurement you can make.

kt_sat_derate.note: Kt at peak current / Kt at low current

_bus_note: These describe what the ACTUATOR accepts. The voltage your robot actually supplies belongs in the joint/application file as bus_voltage.

Rth_ca.note: housing to ambient AS MOUNTED IN YOUR ROBOT, not on a bench

T_winding_max.note: Class A 105, B 130, F 155, H 180; subtract margin

_tn_curve_README: A MEASURED torque-speed envelope: peak output torque vs speed, on a stated
bus. Give one and the tool uses it for the envelope and the no-load speed
instead of computing them from Ke/R_phase/L_phase -- a real curve pins the
whole envelope at once, and L_phase in particular is otherwise a +/-100%
guess. Omit it and everything still works off the computed envelope.
The computed envelope is ALWAYS still reported and plotted alongside as an
independent cross-check, and is never fitted to the curve, so a model that
disagrees shows up instead of being quietly absorbed.
points        [[speed, torque], ...] -- sorted automatically
speed_units   rpm_output (default) | rad_s_output. Rotor-side values must
be converted to the OUTPUT first; a wrong choice here is a
gear-ratio-sized error, so unrecognised units are refused.
torque_units  N.m
bus_voltage   the bus the curve was MEASURED at. If the application runs a
different voltage the speed axis is rescaled by the ratio and
the report flags it -- a first-order fix, not a real curve.
source        vendor | measured (your own dyno) | unavailable
tol           relative uncertainty, e.g. 0.05 for a digitised plot
Set "source": "unavailable" with a note and no points to record that no
trustworthy curve exists -- better than omitting the field, which looks like
nobody checked. Torque is held flat below the first point (that region is
current-limited) and the model takes over above the last.

tn_curve.note: where this came from -- datasheet section, or your test setup

_overload_curves_README: MEASURED overload endurance: how long the actuator held each torque before
its thermal protection stopped it. This is to the THERMAL model what
tn_curve is to the electrical one, and it is the only vendor data that
checks it. Without one, a duty cycle near the thermal limit is being judged
by four estimates in series (Rth_wc, Rth_ca, C_w, C_c).
As with tn_curve the measurement is never fitted to -- the model is run
beside it and the disagreement is reported. That has already earned its
keep: the RobStride RS00's endurance table implies about 2x the copper loss
its own published T-N curve implies, on the same part. A fit would have
hidden that; the cross-check prints it and names the suspect parameter.
Read the ratio column as a safety direction. ratio > 1 means the model
outlasts the measurement, i.e. it is OPTIMISTIC and a verdict built on it
is unsafe. ratio < 1 means it is conservative.
condition          REQUIRED: rotating | stalled. No default -- a stalled
winding heats one phase 1.414x harder than a rotating
one at the same current, so guessing is a 41% error.
Unrecognised or missing values are refused.
points             [[torque_Nm, seconds], ...] -- sorted automatically.
Interpolated log-linearly in time (these span decades);
never extrapolated off either end.
speed_rpm_output   output speed of the test, 0 for stalled. Iron and
friction loss depend on it.
ambient_C          test ambient.
mounting           the test's heat path (free_air | bolted_plastic |
bolted_metal | heatsunk). Rth_ca is re-derived from
this for the comparison, so a bench-heatsink table is
not judged against an in-robot Rth_ca.
rated_torque       the table's own continuous endpoint, if quoted. Shown
as the figure to prefer when the model reads optimistic.
time_units         s (default) | min
torque_units       N.m
source             vendor | measured (your own bench)
tol                relative uncertainty on the durations.
A vendor may publish one table per condition, so this is a LIST. Copy the
test conditions from the datasheet caption verbatim into the note: these
tables are often taken on a smaller heatsink than the rated-torque figure,
which makes them stricter than the headline spec, and a reader needs to know.

overload_curves.note: datasheet section, and the test conditions from its caption

notes: Free-text caveats about how the vendor measured their numbers.
